name: Web Audio playback
plain: Plays generated sound; the audio context stays silent until the person has interacted.
meaning: A site can synthesize and mix sound at sample precision (games, music tools). Autoplay rules keep it quiet until a click, but once resumed it can run for as long as the tab lives.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: Context state suspended until resumed; lives with the page
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
steps: Audio plays through the default output

limits.headline: Can play and mix sound inside the page, after you have tapped
limits.user_action: You tap Play, Start or anything on the page before sound begins.
can: Play sounds, music or game effects that it makes or loads
Mix and change sounds, such as echo and volume
Keep sound going while the tab is open
cannot: Make sound before you have tapped, clicked or pressed a key
Listen through your microphone; that needs a separate permission
Play over a tab you muted yourself

story.what_it_is: A page can make sound, but stays silent until you click or tap.

marketing.name: Autoplay policy in Chrome
marketing.pitch: Chrome explains that sound only plays after you interact with the page.

story.for_you: A game or music tool starts making sound only after your first tap. You are never surprised by blaring audio from a new tab.
story.for_makers: Makers get full control over sound: effects, synths and mixing. The gesture rule is how browsers keep ads from shouting at you.

use_cases.example: A browser game plays footsteps, music and echo effects, all built from code.
A web music maker lets you play synths and drums in the browser.
A video call tool adds noise cancelling to your voice.
A learning site shows how a sound wave works and plays it.
Audio processing can reveal small differences between devices and is used in fingerprinting.
An ad network tries to autoplay a video ad with sound, blocked until you tap.

technical_bounds: AudioContext starts suspended until user activation on the page (Chrome 71, Firefox 66, Safari since webkitAudioContext)
Chrome limits about 6 simultaneously active AudioContexts per tab in older versions; Safari limits 4 on iOS (older)
Cannot choose output device without setSinkId and a permission (selectAudioOutput)
Sample rate and output latency are readable (fingerprint)
Cannot read the system volume or other apps' audio

history.change: AudioContext.setSinkId lets a page route output to a chosen device
